questions.q: What did the Cognitive Revolution give early humans?
a: Better brains that allowed language and cooperation
Larger bodies and much stronger muscles
The ability to farm immediately
A written alphabet and a system of money
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the revolution around 70,000 years ago brought mental development that let humans communicate and work together.

questions.q: Why was language so important for our species?
a: It let people share information and cooperate flexibly
It made hunting tools unnecessary
It ended all conflict between groups
It allowed people to live alone safely
questions.why: Lesson 1 says language spread ideas, helping people share lessons about food and predators and cooperate as a society.

questions.q: What did the Agricultural Revolution lead to?
a: A rapid explosion in population
The end of trade networks
A long decline in food production
The disappearance of language
questions.why: Lesson 1 says farming was more efficient than hunting and gathering and let the population grow dramatically.

questions.q: Why did money and writing become necessary?
a: Barter became inefficient as societies grew
Farmers refused to trade with craftsmen
Governments banned all bartering
People forgot how to make tools
questions.why: Lesson 2 shows barter failing once a farmer might lack a pig or a knife, and how records and currency solved that.

questions.q: What does the summary say about child mortality today?
a: Only about one in 1,000 children dies in childhood
Two or three children die in even rich families
It has stayed the same for centuries
It is higher now than in the past
questions.why: Lesson 3 contrasts the past, when even wealthy families lost children, with today's rate of about one in 1,000.
